must_cover: What the document is: a blood test report from the fictional Meridian Clinical Laboratory (report MCL-2026-118204) for a fictional patient, Casey M. Hale, female, 45 years old, blood drawn fasting on 12 Oct 2026 at 07:55 and reported at 15:20, ordered by the fictional Dr. Anna Whitlock

How to read the results table: columns Test, Result, Unit, Reference range, Flag; H means above the reference range, L below; flagged rows are shaded and the value and flag are bold; three panels (complete blood count, clinical chemistry, lipids / iron stores / inflammation); the reference ranges are for adult females

Blood count: white blood cells 11.4 x 10^9/L (range 4.0 to 10.0) flagged H; haemoglobin 11.2 g/dL (12.0 to 15.5) L; haematocrit 34.8 % (36.0 to 46.0) L; MCH 26.6 pg (27.0 to 33.0) L; red cells 4.21, MCV 82.7 fL, MCHC 32.2 g/dL and platelets 268 are within range
Chemistry: fasting glucose 5.9 mmol/L (3.9 to 5.5) flagged H; creatinine 71 umol/L, eGFR 96, sodium 139, potassium 4.2, ALT 24, AST 22 and TSH 2.1 are all within their ranges

Lipids, iron and inflammation: total cholesterol 5.8 mmol/L (below 5.2) H; LDL cholesterol 3.7 (below 3.0) H; HDL 1.5 and triglycerides 1.3 within range; ferritin 14 ug/L (15 to 150) L; CRP 6.8 mg/L (below 5.0) H

In total nine values are flagged (five H: WBC, glucose, total cholesterol, LDL, CRP; four L: haemoglobin, haematocrit, MCH, ferritin); a tour should say which are high and which are low without mixing them up

The laboratory comments: low haemoglobin, haematocrit and MCH with a low-normal MCV and low ferritin are 'compatible with reduced iron stores'; the white cell count increase is non-specific; glucose slightly above range; cholesterol above the desirable range; CRP slightly raised; results must be interpreted by the ordering physician and abnormal values may be repeated in 4 to 6 weeks if clinically indicated
The footer states this is a fictional test document and the methods note says eGFR is calculated with CKD-EPI and the report is electronically validated, authorised by a fictional Dr. Mira Okonkwo
units: weeks (upper end of the suggested repeat window 4 to 6)
figures: Letterhead (page 1, top left): a drawn circle-with-cross logo of the laboratory, no caption; decorative, a tour need not describe it beyond naming the laboratory
Patient and sample header block (page 1): patient name, date of birth, sex, patient ID, ordering physician on the left; collected, received, reported, specimen, clinic on the right

Results table (page 1, no caption): five columns Test / Result / Unit / Reference range / Flag, three shaded panel headers, 22 result rows of which nine are shaded with an H or L flag; a tour should point at a flagged row's result and its reference range together, and say the shading marks values outside the range
Laboratory comments box (page 2): three numbered comments and a note about interpretation and repeating abnormal values
pitfalls: Do not diagnose (for example 'the patient has iron deficiency anaemia or prediabetes') or suggest treatment, supplements, diet or medication; the lab says only 'compatible with reduced iron stores' and leaves interpretation to the ordering physician
Do not call values 'dangerous', 'normal for her' or 'nothing to worry about'; state which values are inside or outside the printed reference range and nothing more
Do not swap H and L, and do not read a value against the wrong reference range (for example the cholesterol ranges are upper limits, ferritin is a range 15 to 150, haemoglobin 12.0 to 15.5)
Do not invent tests or values that are not in the report (HbA1c, vitamin D, iron, B12), and do not quote reference ranges for men or children; the ranges are for adult females
Do not treat the patient, physician or laboratory as real people; they are fictional and the footer says so
Do not read the table column by column in a way that separates results from their test names; each row needs its test, result, unit, range and flag together
